reason: The only available combination connects the uprising to the demand for freedom and should advance the emancipation goal.
expectation: I expect an account of how enslaved people's uprising turned liberty into a political demand, though the legal outcome may require further steps.

effect: The uprising established enslaved people as active agents pressing for freedom; the next step can follow that demand into law.
reaction: The emphasis on insurgents’ agency is a useful distinction.
reason: The only offered combination connects the political demand to the abolition decrees.
expectation: I expect the decrees to establish abolition in law, though not necessarily full freedom of work or independence.

effect: Abolition became law amid revolution, but its enforcement and effects on daily freedom remain open questions.
reaction: The distinction between legal abolition and lived freedom makes the next question compelling.
reason: The 1801 constitution directly tests whether abolition gave workers a free choice of work.
expectation: I expect cultivation requirements to limit workers’ choices despite the prohibition of slavery.

alternatives.reason: Independence is also a goal, but I want to examine the limits on work first.

effect: Abolition changed legal status, but the cultivation requirement constrained workers’ choices; the remaining question concerns independence.
reaction: The distinction between emancipation and freedom to leave work is meaningful.
reason: The only offered combination addresses the remaining independence goal.
expectation: I expect Haiti’s independence to be distinguished from the earlier abolition of slavery.

effect: Independence ended France’s claim to rule and defended emancipation, without ending all coercion or securing immediate recognition.
reaction: The distinction between independence and complete freedom was a useful conclusion.

mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the 1801 constitution was most worthwhile: it showed how legal abolition could coexist with constrained labour choices.

leastWorthwhile.text: The opening was comparatively predictable: the only available action established the insurgents’ agency before the legal questions developed.

surprise.text: The constitution preserved abolition while requiring plantation cultivation, separating emancipation from freedom to leave work.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the opening sequence offered no meaningful choice; the compatible combinations were supplied by the menu.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how independence and the remaining constraints on freedom developed; their distinction made the conclusion interesting.
